newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower for second day.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower for second day.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower for the second day Wednesday, slipping back after the monthly OTC options expiry, the uptrends in gold and silver of the past few weeks are seen intact.

"Gold volatilities remain compressed and that's probably a good reason to buy for an eventual upside breakout, but there's no reason to rush into it," Credit Lyonnais Rouse's New York based chief dealer, Scott Mehlman, said.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.00 an ounce at $393.00, after trading in a $394.10-392.90 range, with support around $393.00 now being tested, traders said.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted at $387.90/388.40, from a London afternoon fix Wednesday at $388.50, and a New York close Tuesday at $388.80/389.20.
"Japanese demand for precious metals has been down this year, because of the strong U.S. dollar, but the Australian dollar has been strong, prompting Australian producer buybacks," Mehlman noted.
Japanese gold imports totalled 11.97 tonnes in July, down 49 percent from July last year, the Japanese Finance Ministry said Thursday.
For the first seven months of 1996, total gold imports were 95.55 tonnes against 178.73 tonnes in the same period last year.
Japanese silver imports in July were also down on last year, with silver imports totalling 656.98 tonnes for the first seven months this year, against 892.00 last year.
COMEX September silver ended down 6.600 cents at $5.172, ahead of its first notice day Friday, and the now active December contract ended down 6.600 cents at $5.251.

"We saw some trade buying ahead of the options expiry, but then precious metals sold off and remain a little nervous," Pell Brothers floor trader Don Tierney said. "The September/December roll is accelerating again and there's also some position squaring going on ahead of the long holiday weekend coming up."
New York markets are closed next Monday for the U.S. Labor Day holiday, while London markets remain open.
NYMEX October platinum closed down $2.10 an ounce at $403.00, while NYMEX December palladium, now the active contract, ended up $0.20 at $128.15.

Japanese platinum imports rose 4.1 percent in July to 6.92 tonnes from 6.65 tonnes in July 1995. Platinum imports in the first seven months this year were 41.97 tonnes, against 42.41 tonnes last year.
Japanese palladium imports were down in July though, compared to last year and totalled 48.16 tonnes in the first seven months of this year, against 58.90 tonnes last year.
